name: The Plumb Line
subtitle: Malaysia Leader Accountability Index
tagline: One yardstick. Every leader. Recorded facts only.
_comment_status: status=framework means NO leader is RANKED yet. M0 published the instrument with zero subjects; M1 (v0.2.0) ingested the first real cited subjects but they remain below ranking validity (see `validity`), so no composite or rank is published. status flips to 'live' only at M2 once a comparable peer set clears the validity thresholds and the bias audit passes.

firewall.rule: Every input is a RECORDED PUBLIC FACT or a standard index computed on recorded public facts. No figure may originate from the Malaysia political simulation engine's predictions or any model inference.
firewall.enforcedBy: scripts/validate-leaderboard.mjs (every metric must carry a primary-source citation object) and scripts/build-leaderboard.mjs (no engine imports).

A.name: Public Record
A.summary: Recorded public facts. No judgement. Every value traces to a primary source.

B.name: Editorial Panel
B.summary: A fixed, published rubric for conduct records cannot capture. Anchored 0-4 ordinal scales. Every score carries a cited justification. Always shown WITH and WITHOUT this layer.

C.name: Composite Political-Science
C.summary: Established indices applied symmetrically, computed on public facts only.

dimensions.name: Legislative output
dimensions.description: Bills, motions, and parliamentary questions sponsored and advanced through the legislative process, weighted by significance and normalized to the applicable peer mean.
dimensions.method: Volden-Wiseman Legislative Effectiveness Score: fraction of items at each of five stages (introduced, committee, beyond committee, passed chamber, enacted), significance-weighted alpha=1 (commemorative) / beta=5 (substantive) / gamma=10 (substantive and significant), normalized so the applicable peer set averages 1.0, then mapped to 0-100.

dimensions.name: Presence and participation
dimensions.description: Attendance, division (vote) participation, and substantive debate contributions in the relevant chamber.
dimensions.method: IPU Indicators for Democratic Parliaments and the Mzalendo report-card model: attendance rate, share of divisions voted, count of substantive Hansard interventions, each normalized within the applicable peer set.

dimensions.name: Pledge fulfilment
dimensions.description: Manifesto and portfolio commitments coded fully / partially / not fulfilled, against the denominator the leader was actually positioned to deliver.
dimensions.method: Thomson et al. (2017) comparative pledge methodology. Each pledge independently coded full / partial / not. Government and opposition are scored against different applicable denominators (an opposition member cannot enact a government pledge); the asymmetry is explicit, not hidden. Score = weighted fulfilment rate within applicable denominator.

dimensions.name: Fiscal stewardship
dimensions.description: Budget execution and audited cost performance for portfolios or governments under the leader's responsibility.
dimensions.method: World Bank and IPU oversight frameworks. Budget execution rate and audited cost-overrun findings under the leader's portfolio, normalized within the applicable peer set. Applies only to those with executive budget authority.

dimensions.name: Integrity and transparency record
dimensions.description: Asset-declaration compliance, register-of-interests completeness, and the factual STATUS of any court or anti-corruption matters of public record.
dimensions.method: Parliamentary codes-of-conduct standards. Records the factual status only (declared / not declared; charged / convicted / acquitted / discharged). NEVER an editorial verdict on guilt. An unresolved or dropped matter is recorded as such, not as a finding.
dimensions.guardrail: 3R-adjacent and integrity claims require two independent primary sources (CLAUDE.md Accuracy Standard). A claim that cannot meet this bar is dropped, not softened.
dimensions.attributionRule: Added v0.2.0 after the M1 dry-run. A5 records the SUBJECT'S OWN status only. A court matter involving the leader's staff, family member, business associate, or party colleague is NOT the leader's status and is never recorded against them — guilt by association is an overclaim and a defamation risk. The default status for a leader with no personal matter of record is 'none-on-record', scored identically to 'declared/acquitted' (no penalty for the absence of wrongdoing).

dimensions.name: Crisis handling
dimensions.description: Demonstrated handling of a discrete public crisis within the leader's remit.
dimensions.method: Anchored 0-4 ordinal scale with published descriptors. Each score cites the specific dated event it rests on.

ordinalAnchors.0: Worsened the crisis or evaded responsibility on the public record.
ordinalAnchors.2: Adequate, documented response with mixed outcomes.
ordinalAnchors.4: Documented, decisive response with measurable resolution.

sourceType: Named outlet citing a primary source

dimensions.name: Reform delivered vs promised
dimensions.description: Whether structural reforms the leader championed were enacted, diluted, or abandoned.
dimensions.method: Anchored 0-4 ordinal scale. Distinct from A3 pledge fulfilment: this scores the SUBSTANCE and durability of a reform, not the binary of a pledge. Every score cites the gazetted instrument or its absence.

ordinalAnchors.0: Championed reform then abandoned or reversed it.
ordinalAnchors.2: Partial reform enacted with material dilution.
ordinalAnchors.4: Reform gazetted and operative as promised.

dimensions.name: Consensus and institution-building
dimensions.description: Documented work to build cross-bench, federal, or institutional consensus rather than zero-sum capture.
dimensions.method: Anchored 0-4 ordinal scale. Scores documented process behaviour (joint committees formed, bipartisan instruments co-signed), never the leader's political alignment.

ordinalAnchors.0: Documented institutional capture or norm erosion.
ordinalAnchors.2: Worked within institutions without strengthening them.
ordinalAnchors.4: Documented strengthening of an institution or cross-bench instrument.

dimensions.name: Candor on reversals
dimensions.description: Honesty when reversing a stated position: acknowledged and explained, or denied and obscured.
dimensions.method: Anchored 0-4 ordinal scale. Scores transparency of the reversal, not the reversal itself (changing course on evidence is legitimate).

ordinalAnchors.0: Reversed a position while denying the reversal on the record.
ordinalAnchors.4: Reversed and explained the reasons on the public record.

dimensions.name: Process discipline (restraint from 3R-baiting)
dimensions.description: Restraint from inflaming Race, Religion, or Royalty for political advantage on the public record.
dimensions.method: Anchored 0-4 ordinal scale measuring PROCESS conduct, never belief or identity. Scores documented instances of de-escalation versus documented incitement findings. This is the only place 3R enters the instrument, and it enters as a discipline metric applied identically to all.

ordinalAnchors.0: Documented finding of inflaming 3R for advantage.
ordinalAnchors.4: Documented, dated act of de-escalating a 3R flashpoint.

dimensions.guardrail: Scores the act, never the actor's community or belief. A negative score requires a documented regulator/court finding, not commentary.

dimensions.name: Pivotality
dimensions.description: Structural voting power in the leader's coalition or chamber.
dimensions.method: Shapley-Shubik power index computed from ACTUAL seat counts (public record). Already used in dossier D001. Measures structural weight, not popularity.
dimensions.neutralityNote: Pivotality is descriptive, not normative. High structural power is neither good nor bad; it contextualizes how much the other dimensions matter.

dimensions.name: Governance indicators (domain-scoped)
dimensions.description: V-Dem-style governance indicators, scoped strictly to the components the leader's office actually touches.
dimensions.method: Only the V-Dem-style indicators within the leader's actual remit are scored (e.g. an electoral-affairs portfolio is scored on clean-election indicators; a justice portfolio on judicial-constraint indicators). Out-of-remit indicators are N/A, never imputed.

dimensions.name: Legislative-network centrality
dimensions.description: Co-sponsorship and coalition-voting centrality in the public division record.
dimensions.method: Network centrality computed from public co-sponsorship and division-voting records. Measures collaborative reach, normalized within the applicable peer set.

roleClasses.name: Backbencher
roleClasses.note: MP without executive or frontbench office.

roleClasses.name: Sub-national executive
roleClasses.note: State Premier / Menteri Besar / Chief Minister.

comparability.rule: Each leader is scored only on dimensions applicable to their role(s) over the scored period, normalized WITHIN their applicable peer set, then mapped to the common 0-100 scale. Readers compare like-with-like via the role class; the headline index stays cross-comparable via normalization.
comparability.periodBasedScoring: A leader whose role changes mid-period is scored per-period under each applicable class (e.g. Economy Minister period, then backbencher period), then time-weighted.
comparability.benchmarks: Foreign benchmark leaders run through the identical instrument, role classes, and normalization. They are labelled calibration anchors, not competitors. A benchmark scoring badly on a dimension is shown honestly.

normalization.missingDataRationale: A metric with no public record is N/A. Imputing 0 or the mean would smuggle in a hidden judgement. Per-leader coverage % is published.

validity._comment: Added in v0.2.0 after the M1 dry-run on the first real subjects. These thresholds make the instrument REFUSE to publish a misleading score rather than produce a false-precise one. A leader can be on file (data ingested, cited, displayed) without being ranked.
validity.minPeerSetRationale: A dimension is only normalized when its applicable peer set has at least this many defined values. Min-max or rank normalization on one or two points is meaningless: a lone value rank-normalizes to 0, so Singapore's 100th-percentile governance would display as 0. Below the floor the dimension is marked 'insufficient-peer-set' and excluded from the composite — not scored as zero.
validity.minCoverageRationale: A leader receives a published composite and rank only when at least half their applicable dimensions carry a valid (peer-normalized) score. Below the floor the leader is listed as 'on file, not yet rankable', their cited raw metrics shown for transparency, but no composite or rank asserted. This is what prevents a governing-centric index from emitting a misleadingly low number for an opposition figure whose applicable dimensions are mostly uncovered.
validity.notRankedDisplay: Leaders below either threshold appear in an 'On file, awaiting a comparable cohort' section with their recorded, cited metrics visible and an explicit reason, never with a composite or rank.

jurisdictionDataGaps._comment: Jurisdiction-aware applicability (M2 decision, 2026-06-01). A dimension listed here is one the jurisdiction does not publish the source data for AT ALL — it is applicable to the role but unsourceable for any subject of that country. Such a dimension is excluded from BOTH scoring and the coverage denominator for that country's subjects, and is DISCLOSED on every affected leader's detail as 'excluded — jurisdiction data gap', never silently dropped. This stops a transparency gap in the source country from permanently barring otherwise-documented leaders from ranking, without imputing a fabricated value. Each exclusion is reviewed and removed the moment the data becomes available. Excluding a dimension a leader simply lacks a record on (vs. one the whole jurisdiction never publishes) is NOT permitted here — that remains an honest coverage gap.

MY.reason: The Malaysian Parliament does not publish per-member attendance or division (vote) records (A2), and no machine-readable co-sponsorship / division-network dataset exists (C3). Both are applicable to the role but structurally unsourceable for any Malaysian subject as of 2026-06-01.

aggregation.crossLayerRationale: Cross-layer score is the mean of (a) the weighted arithmetic mean of layer scores and (b) their weighted geometric mean. This halfway form follows the V-Dem electoral-democracy aggregation: it allows partial compensation between layers but punishes a catastrophic failure in any one, so strong legislative output cannot fully buy back an integrity collapse.

audit.summary: Five gates, all standard composite-indicator quality assurance. The Bias-Audited badge renders only when all pass. The audit report is signed and reader-verifiable.

gates.name: Symmetry
gates.test: Identical metric set, weights, and normalization config applied to all subjects. Zero per-leader overrides.

gates.name: Source coverage
gates.test: Every non-N/A metric value carries a primary-source citation object.

gates.name: Partisan-signal test
gates.test: Whether Layer B adds party/coalition-correlated variance beyond Layer A. Computed as the correlation between coalition affiliation and the (Layer B minus Layer A) residual.
gates.fails: Residual-coalition correlation exceeds the threshold. The panel is leaking bias.

gates.name: Rank robustness
gates.test: Saisana/Saltelli sensitivity analysis: perturb weights across reasonable ranges and record rank stability. Unstable ranks are published as uncertainty INTERVALS, never false-precise integers.
gates.fails: Never fails the build; converts unstable point ranks into published rank ranges.

gates.name: Inter-coder reliability
gates.test: Krippendorff's alpha on Layer B ordinal scores across coders.
gates.fails: A Layer B criterion below the alpha threshold is demoted to 'insufficient agreement' and excluded, not averaged.

exclusions.name: Race, Religion, Royalty
exclusions.rationale: Excluded by design. The only adjacency is B5, which scores PROCESS restraint, never belief or identity.

exclusions.name: Popularity, polls, social-media following, charisma
exclusions.rationale: Popularity is not accountability. Excluded entirely.

exclusions.name: Policy direction or ideology
exclusions.rationale: We never reward or punish a political position. We score only delivery against the leader's OWN stated commitments and the integrity of conduct. This is the core non-partisanship guarantee.

exclusions.name: Rumor, unproven allegation, anonymous sourcing
exclusions.rationale: Fails the Accuracy Standard. Dropped, not softened.

exclusions.name: Private life
exclusions.rationale: Out of scope. Only public conduct in public office is measured.
